editorial.headline: Keeping Cultural Heritage Intact, in Physical and Digital Form
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the careful preservation, restoration and digital continuity of cultural heritage—and remains open to full foreign ownership nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is about preserving cultural heritage before loss becomes irreversible. It includes preventive conservation, curative conservation and restoration, together with consultancy that considers both the tangible and intangible significance of heritage and its sustainability. The scope is deliberately broad across materials and surfaces: movable and immovable archaeological assets, leather, archival documents, graphic and printed documents, wooden panels, art objects, ceramic tiles, goldsmith work, canvas and mural paintings, photography, sculpture, textiles and embroidery, stained glass, and scientific and industrial objects all sit within it.

It also recognises that preservation now has a digital dimension. Digitising movable and immovable heritage, gathering data, managing collections, creating virtual replicas and using other digital means to secure heritage preservation are all part of the activity. A business registering here is therefore framed around the stewardship of cultural material and its continuity, whether the work concerns a physical object, a collection, or its durable digital record. The slim record does not state any enterprise-scale categories open to this activity, so it provides no basis for assigning it to a particular business scale.

At the national level, the position is straightforward: foreign investment is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record does not impose a reduced foreign share for this activity. The practical significance is clear: an investor may structure a PMA registration around cultural-heritage conservation, restoration and its supporting digital work without a national foreign-equity cap below full ownership.

Bali requires its own reading, but the current record is not a prohibition. Its status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the activity described as medium-high or high risk and therefore not blocked by the provincial moratorium; the address must still be verified. The Bali moratorium permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island, under the cited Governor’s letter. This activity is recorded outside that blocked risk band, so a foreign investor can register it in Bali today, subject to address-specific verification rather than an island-wide moratorium bar.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not block this activity under its PMA moratorium, but the business address still needs verification.
